 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The New York Yankees are bringing back one of their most important bullpen arms for the 2027 MLB season. Closer David Bednar has accepted the team's qualifying offer, agreeing to a one-year, $23.15 million contract, according to ESPN.
 The decision gives New York some important stability in the back end of its bullpen heading into the offseason. It is somewhat of a surprising decision for Bednar, who could have opted for free agency and been arguably the best closer on the market.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Predicting MLB free agent landing spots in 2026-27 offseason 
 David Bednar accepts Yankees qualifying offer
 Oct 7, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees relief pitcher David Bednar (53) reacts after the final out of the game for the win over the Toronto Blue Jays in the ninth inning during game three of the ALDS round for the 2025 MLB playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images
 Bednar will return to the Yankees after delivering an impressive 2026 campaign. The right-hander recorded 35 saves in 39 opportunities, posting a 2.47 ERA across 69 1/3 innings.
 The 32-year-old was acquired from the Pittsburgh Pirates in July 2025 and quickly became an important part of New York's bullpen. Since joining the Yankees, he has recorded a 2.39 ERA and 45 saves, establishing himself as the team's preferred option in the ninth inning.
 New York extended the qualifying offer to Bednar on Nov. 2, giving him until Tuesday, Nov. 17, to decide whether to accept the one-year contract. The $23.15 million offer represented a significant guaranteed salary for the upcoming season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yankees secure key piece of bullpen for 2027
 Oct 1, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees relief pitcher David Bednar (53) celebrates after the game against the Boston Red Sox during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2025 MLB playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
 Bednar's decision is an important development for a Yankees team that entered the offseason with several bullpen questions. New York has been looking to retain some of its experienced relievers while identifying additional options to strengthen the group.
 Keeping Bednar gives the Yankees an established closer who already understands the organization and has experience pitching in high-pressure situations in New York.
 The Yankees' bullpen was one of the team's strengths during the 2026 regular season, and retaining Bednar helps preserve an important part of that group. His return also gives manager Aaron Boone a clearer picture of how the late innings could look next season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rather than entering free agency and searching for a replacement at closer, New York now has its ninth-inning option secured for 2027. Bednar's acceptance of the qualifying offer gives the Yankees some much-needed certainty as the organization continues working through its offseason plans.
